lines: The Executive floor. Been awhile since I was here.
[worried] I need to do this fast and save Betty.
Yuvie: Donnie. The Executive floor. Look at you, moving up in the world.
Yuvie: The deal stands. Overheat the server room and Betty is free.
Donnie[angry]: Then tell me how I get in.
Irshad: The door takes a code. A new one every morning, and every morning it belongs to a different member of staff.
Adi: And it's encrypted! Which means—
Yuvie: You'll need an executive keycard to decrypt it. Liam is on your floor. By the windows. He has one.
Donnie[shocked]: Liam. The CEO's son. Will he do it.
Yuvie: He wants this over as much as you do. Ask nicely or find another way I don't know.
The line goes dead.
Donnie: Liam.
Liam[angry]: Don't. Don't say my name on this floor. Do you know how many cameras are up here?
Donnie: Your people say I need your keycard. To decrypt the server room code.
Liam[angry]: My keycard. On a decryption log. With my name on it. On the day my father's servers cook.
Liam[angry]: Fuck off, Donnie. Do what you were told and leave me out of it.
Donnie[angry]: I am doing what I was told. This is the part where I need your card.
Liam[angry]: One more word and I make one phone call. Guess who it's about.
Liam: ...Go mop something.
[angry] He's not handing it over. Not if I ask nicely, anyway.
Something hot. In the face. The lounge vending machine does hot coffee.
Coffee costs coins. And executives drop change in the plant pots.
Liam[angry]: Are you still here? Go. Mop. Something.
The coffee's in my pocket. Terrible place for coffee. (Press its number to hold it.)
A coin. Buried in the soil like treasure.
Another one. These people don't pick up anything they drop.
Three coins. That's a coffee.
Just soil now. Very expensive soil.
A plant. Healthier than me.
Hot coffee: three coins. I've got {n}.
Hot coffee. Extra hot. Let me take the lid off.
Not for drinking.
One coffee's plenty. I'm not here for the caffeine.
Hot drinks and snacks. Executive prices.
Donnie: Liam. Coffee?
Liam[angry]: I said f—
Splash.
Liam[shocked]: AAAGH! MY FACE! MY— THIS SHIRT IS ITALIAN!
Liam[angry]: You're DEAD, janitor!
[worried] Run. The small meeting room round the corner: there's a locker in there, and the door locks from the outside.
Not in there. One way in, one way out, no locker. He'd have me.
Stand and wait for the lift doors with him behind me? No.
Liam[angry]: Donnie? I know you're in here.
Click.
Liam[shocked]: ...Did you just lock me in?
Donnie: You're well aware. Aren't you?
Liam[angry]: Open this door. Right now.
Donnie: Keycard. Under the door.
Liam[angry]: Do you have ANY idea who I am? One call and Betty is dead.
Donnie: You will turn a janitor into a murderer Liam. I doubt that you even want to be a murderer in the first place.
Liam[angry]: ...
Liam: If I give you the card, you let me out. I don't want to be stuck here while you use my keycard.
Donnie: If you give me the card, I'll think about it.
A keycard slides out under the door. It's still a bit damp.
Liam[angry]: Use it once. Do nothing more than what's told. And when this is over, you and I are going to have a conversation.
Donnie: We'll see...
Liam[angry]: Donnie? Are you done? I can hear you out there! Open this door!
Donnie: No.
You got caught. Liam beats the living crap out of you.
The CEO got you. He doesn't stand anyone who betrays him.
Security got you. Betty doesn't have that long.
INSERT and DELETE. Writing things, and wiping them out.
KODEX says I won't need them on this floor. It didn't say anything about the next one.
No power. Dead screen.
The staff directory. This machine just serves one table, 'staff', to the rest of the floor.
Nothing to do on it. Other computers can read it, if the link station points them here.
The badge register. One table, 'badges', served to the rest of the floor.
Nothing to do on it. Other computers can read it, if the link station points them here.
Priya Shah. Head of Security Systems. Today's code is hers.
Funny. Her desk looked empty this morning.
Marcus Hale, Network Manager. Covering for Priya, so today it's his code. Lucky Marcus.
V, Q, 3, L. No keypad on earth takes that. It's still scrambled.
The link station in Executive office A decrypts things. With a keycard.
The link station. Every computer on this floor talks to the network through this one.
Each machine can be pointed at one other machine. Then it can read that machine's table as well as its own.
And there's a keycard reader on the side: DECRYPT.
LINK STATION  ·  Executive network
Which computer?
Point it at:
A pen drive, taped under the drawer. Label: 'KEYS - DO NOT LOSE'.
Nothing up here prints anything. Executives don't print; they have people.
HR's printer room. One floor down.
Stationery. Very expensive stationery.
Drive in. Print. The printer, for once in its life, just prints.
A key map: which column points at which, on every computer on the Executive floor.
Emergency kit. A torch. Batteries included, for once.
Plasters, a foil blanket and a whistle. I'm not whistling.
Decrypt what? I haven't got anything to decrypt yet.
DECRYPT: insert executive keycard.
Liam's got one.
DECRYPT: 'Operator badge needs server room clearance.'
My badge. The employee terminal at reception sorts that.
Liam's card in. VQ3L in.
{music:framed}DECRYPTION KEY: L. ———  ...REVOKED.
INCIDENT REPORTED: OFFICE OF THE CEO.
[shocked] Oh, no.
CEO[stern]: What the fuck! Liam's keycard is used on my link station. I knew he would pull shit like this
CEO[angry]: What is he up to though?
CEO[stern]: Security. Kill the lights on three and lock the stairwell. Nobody leaves this floor with my data.
CEO[angry]: And if it is my son, I want to see his face when you find him.
Clunk. The Executive floor goes dark.
Donnie[shocked]: He disabled his own son's keycard.
Donnie: He doesn't trust his own son. ...Bruh.
[worried] Security on the stairs, and the CEO himself out on the floor.
If Liam's card is dead, the CEO's own card won't be. And his office is open now. He left in a hurry.
The link station's on backup power, and nobody's looking in here. This office is safe, at least.
Torch on. Quietly.
I need a torch. The emergency cabinet. Right here in this office.
Dark: F flicks the torch to lure them away. Hide in plants. Executive office A is safe.
His keycard. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like the building.
Of course it is.
A paperweight shaped like the building. Subtle.
His laptop's still awake. Inbox open.
From the Board: 'MagiCorp shares are at 83p. Their tech is fine. They're waiting for a client to fall into their lap.'
From Helena Voss, CFO: 'If we ever have one bad day, MagiCorp has our clients by the evening. Make sure we never have one.'
From the analysts: 'MAGI: dormant, not dead. The right boost and it doubles overnight. Possibly more.'
[shocked] MagiCorp is just waiting for GyaraCorp to fall over. And I could maybe push it.
And Ryker's MagiCorp login is still written on my hand.
MagiCorp. Waiting for somebody else's bad day. Good luck to them.
MagiCorp at 83p. Waiting for a push.
The CEO's card in. The station hums. And my phone—
[shocked] ...restarts itself. Now? NOW?
A software update. In a blackout. With the CEO hunting me.
The call app works now, apparently.
[worried] A bank app. MagiCorp at 83p a share. And I know exactly what's about to happen to GyaraCorp.
VQ3L, decrypted: 7302.
Today's server room code.
7302. I've got it. The server room's on the right.
Everything. Betty's college pot. Into a company worth 83p a share.
[worried] It'd better be worth it.
SERVER ROOM. Authorised personnel. A keypad, and a code that changes every morning.
I don't have today's.
Yuvie: Donnie. You've gone quiet. Where are you?
Donnie: Outside the server room.
Yuvie: And? Can you get in?
Tell them the truth?
Truth: "I've got the code. I'm going in."
Lie: "The code's dead. I can't get in."
Donnie: I've got today's code. I'm going in.
Yuvie: Good. Ten minutes and it's over. Then Betty goes home.
Adi: Probably.
Irshad: Adi.
Adi: Definitely! Definitely goes home.
Donnie: The code's wrong. It's dead. I can't get in.
Yuvie: ...
Yuvie: Then you'd better find another way, Donnie. Quickly.
The line goes dead.
[angry] Seven. Three. Zero. Two.
The door opens.
Not in there. In the dark, with them out here, a room is just a box with me in it.
The lift's dead and the stairwell's locked. He thought of everything.
My spare cart. Every floor has one. Nobody notices a janitor with a cart.
Mops, buckets, bin bags.
Security: Executive floor. Mind the marble.
Security: Another day, another very expensive corridor.
Security: Don't touch the art. Any of it. Some of it's the walls.
Security: Quiet today. I like quiet.
Security: Hold on. Janitor? Where's your cart?
Security: No cart, no business up here. Back to the lift.
Assistant: He wants the deck by noon. It's eleven fifty-eight.
Assistant: If anyone asks, I'm in a meeting. I'm always in a meeting.
Assistant: Excuse me. Those are executive computers.
Assistant: Out. Now. Please. Thank you.
Executive: If this coffee isn't single origin I'm calling somebody.
Executive: Do you know what I earn? Neither do I. It's a lot.
CEO: THERE you are.
CEO: Stop right there.
CEO: Liam? Come out and explain yourself.
CEO: Whoever you are, you're fired. Whatever you are.
CEO: I built this floor. I know every corner of it.
CEO: I can hear you breathing. Breathe less expensively.
Security: Oi! Stop right there!
Security: Got one!
Liam's card is dead. The CEO's won't be.
His office. Top left. Open now.
Hide in the locker. Liam only sees what's in his cone: wait till he's searching the far end, slip out, lock the door.
And there's an INFI Bank app I didn't ask for.
